title: Fastest Ascent of Mount Everest (South Side, with O2)
description: Lhakpa Gelu Sherpa ascended from Everest South Base Camp to the 8,848m summit in an officially documented 10 hours, 56 minutes, and 46 seconds on May 26, 2003. This achievement was certified by Guinness World Records and reaffirmed by Nepal's Ministry of Tourism following a 2017 Supreme Court verification review.
label: Verified Record
source: Guinness World Records / Nepal Ministry of Tourism

title: Most Summits of Mount Everest
description: Kami Rita Sherpa holds the world record for the most successful ascents of Mount Everest, reaching the summit for the 32nd time on May 17, 2026 at age 56. First summiting in 1994, he has spent over three decades leading elite expedition teams and fixing summit lines.
label: Verified Record
source: The Himalayan Database / Nepal Department of Tourism

title: Youngest Person to Summit Mount Everest
description: American mountaineer Jordan Romero reached the summit of Mount Everest via the Tibetan North Ridge on May 22, 2010, aged 13 years, 10 months, and 10 days. Climbing with his father Paul Romero, Karen Lundgren, and three Sherpa guides, the feat is verified by the China Tibet Mountaineering Association.
label: Verified Record

title: Oldest Man to Summit Mount Everest
description: Japanese alpinist Yuichiro Miura reached the summit of Mount Everest on May 23, 2013, at the verified age of 80 years and 223 days, becoming the oldest man in history to stand on top of the world. Miura previously completed successful summits at ages 70 and 75.
label: Verified Record

title: First Person to Climb All 14 Eight-Thousanders
description: South Tyrolean mountaineer Reinhold Messner became the first person to summit all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks without supplemental oxygen between 1970 and 1986. His achievement was comprehensively verified by the UIAA, the Himalayan Database, and modern chronological terrain registers.
label: Verified Record

title: First Woman to Summit Mount Everest
description: Japanese mountaineer Junko Tabei made history on May 16, 1975, by becoming the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest via the Southeast Ridge, climbing with Ang Tsering Sherpa as part of the Japanese Ladies Everest Expedition. She subsequently became the first woman to summit the Seven Summits.
label: Verified Record
source: The Himalayan Database / Japanese Alpine Club

title: First Ascent of Everest Without Supplemental Oxygen
description: Reinhold Messner and Austrian climber Peter Habeler reached the summit of Mount Everest on May 8, 1978, without bottled oxygen, disproving the prevailing medical consensus that severe hypoxia in the death zone would cause irreversible brain damage and fatal pulmonary collapse.
label: Verified Record

title: First Solo Ascent of Mount Everest
description: Reinhold Messner achieved the first completely solo ascent of Mount Everest on August 20, 1980, ascending via a new route on the North Face from Tibet without supplemental oxygen, pre-placed camps, or radio communication during the heavy monsoon season.
label: Verified Record
source: The Alpine Journal / The Himalayan Database

title: Fastest Ascent of All 14 Eight-Thousanders (with O2)
description: Norwegian alpinist Kristin Harila and Nepali mountain guide Tenjen Lama Sherpa climbed all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks in 92 days (between April 26 and July 27, 2023), completing verified true summits on every peak and establishing the current officially recognized speed benchmark.
label: Verified Record
source: Guinness World Records / The Himalayan Database

title: First Winter Ascent of K2
description: A collaborative team of ten Nepali climbers led by Nirmal Purja and Mingma Gyalje Sherpa achieved the historic first winter ascent of K2 (8,611m) on January 16, 2021. Ten meters below the summit, all ten climbers waited for each other to step onto the summit together while singing the national anthem of Nepal.
label: Verified Record
source: Alpine Club of Pakistan / American Alpine Journal

title: First Woman to Climb All 14 Eight-Thousanders Without O2
description: Austrian mountaineer Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner became the first woman to climb all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks without supplemental oxygen, completing her quest on August 23, 2011 on K2 via the demanding North Pillar from China. All 14 of her ascents were verified true geographical summits.
label: Verified Record

title: Fastest Seven Summits (Male, including Carstensz)
description: Australian climber Steven Plain set the Guinness World Record for the fastest completion of the Seven Summits (male, including Carstensz) in 117 days, 6 hours, and 50 minutes between January 18 and May 14, 2018. To comprehensively satisfy both the Messner and Bass lists, Plain climbed both Carstensz Pyramid and Mount Kosciuszko, finishing on Mount Everest.
label: Verified Record

title: First Blind Person to Summit Mount Everest
description: American athlete Erik Weihenmayer became the first blind person to reach the summit of Mount Everest on May 25, 2001. Guided by teammates using bells and verbal rope cues, he navigated the treacherous Khumbu Icefall and Hillary Step, later completing the Seven Summits in 2008.
label: Verified Record

title: All 14 Eight-Thousanders Without O2 (First American / 6th Overall)
description: Ed Viesturs became the first American and the sixth person in history to climb all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks without supplemental oxygen. Completing his 16-year 'Endeavor 8000' project on Annapurna on May 12, 2005, he adhered strictly to his philosophy: 'Getting to the top is optional; getting down is mandatory.'
label: Verified Record
source: American Alpine Club / The Himalayan Database

title: Fastest Female Ascent of Mount Everest
description: Hong Kong mountaineer Ada Tsang Yin-hung reached the summit of Mount Everest from South Base Camp in 25 hours and 50 minutes on May 23, 2021, setting the fastest verified female speed ascent recorded by the Nepal Department of Tourism and certified by Guinness World Records.
label: Verified Record
source: Guinness World Records / Nepal Department of Tourism

title: First Winter Ascent of Nanga Parbat
holder: Simone Moro, Alex Txikon & Muhammad Ali Sadpara
description: Italian alpinist Simone Moro, Basque climber Alex Txikon, and Pakistani high-altitude legend Muhammad Ali Sadpara achieved the historic first winter ascent of Nanga Parbat (8,126m) on February 26, 2016 via the Kinshofer route, overcoming over three decades of failed winter attempts.
label: Verified Record
source: Alpine Club of Pakistan / Italian Alpine Club (CAI)
